question: Business Process Re-engineering (BPR) primarily focuses on:

options.text: Fundamental redesign of business processes to achieve major improvements
Incremental correction of individual coding defects
Converting source code into machine code
Replacing every application with a purchased package

explanation: BPR radically rethinks and redesigns business processes to achieve substantial improvements in performance, cost, quality, or service.

question: Which statement best distinguishes software re-engineering from ordinary software maintenance?

options.text: Re-engineering examines and transforms an existing system to improve it while preserving useful functionality
Maintenance never changes existing source code
Re-engineering always creates a completely new system from scratch
Re-engineering is limited to correcting syntax errors

explanation: Software re-engineering analyzes and transforms an existing system to improve its structure or maintainability, often retaining its functionality.

question: A legacy application is analyzed, its design is recovered, and its code is reorganized without intentionally changing its external behavior. This is best described as:

options.text: Software restructuring
Forward engineering
Domain engineering
Business process re-engineering

explanation: Restructuring reorganizes an existing system or its representations while generally preserving external behavior.

question: Which activity is most specifically associated with code restructuring?

options.text: Improving the organization of source code while preserving its intended behavior
Deriving reusable components for an entire domain
Building a new system solely from new requirements
Redefining the organization's business strategy

explanation: Code restructuring changes code organization or form to improve readability or maintainability without intended functional change.

question: Forward engineering is best described as:

options.text: Developing or rebuilding a system from requirements and design toward implementation
Recovering higher-level design information from source code only
Removing all documentation from a legacy system
Measuring only the amount of reused code

explanation: Forward engineering proceeds from higher-level specifications or designs toward implementation.

question: Which statement correctly contrasts reverse engineering and forward engineering?

options.text: Reverse engineering derives higher-level representations from an existing system; forward engineering builds toward implementation
Reverse engineering is only testing, while forward engineering is only maintenance
Both always begin with business requirements and end at source code
Forward engineering recovers design from code, while reverse engineering creates new code from design

explanation: Reverse engineering works from an existing implementation toward abstractions; forward engineering proceeds toward implementation.

question: A team converts unstructured code into modules, simplifies control flow, and standardizes data structures, but keeps the system's externally visible results unchanged. The main goal is:

options.text: Improve internal structure and maintainability
Change the business process completely
Increase functional scope in every module
Replace the domain model with a new business domain

explanation: Restructuring aims to improve internal organization while preserving intended behavior.

question: Which situation most strongly motivates software re-engineering?

options.text: A new small application has no users yet
A business-critical legacy system still works but is difficult and costly to maintain
The only objective is to add one new report to a well-structured system
A system must be discarded despite being easy to maintain

explanation: Re-engineering is often considered when a valuable legacy system remains useful but has become hard to maintain or evolve.

question: Which activity is most likely to be part of a software re-engineering process?

options.text: Ignoring the existing system's behavior and user needs
Inventory analysis, document restructuring, reverse engineering, code restructuring, and forward engineering
Deleting the source code before analysis
Skipping testing because the system already exists

explanation: Common re-engineering activities include assessing assets, recovering understanding, restructuring representations, and validating the result.

question: Why should a re-engineered system undergo regression testing?

options.text: To prove that no future maintenance will be needed
To check that restructuring has not unintentionally changed existing behavior
To measure the number of developers in the team
To automatically generate all business requirements

explanation: Regression testing checks whether existing functionality continues to work after internal changes.

question: Which statement about BPR and software re-engineering is most accurate?

options.text: BPR is only a method for renaming variables
BPR focuses on redesigning business processes, while software re-engineering focuses on transforming existing software assets
Software re-engineering always changes the business process, while BPR never involves technology
Both terms mean exactly the same activity

explanation: BPR targets business-process redesign; software re-engineering targets analysis and transformation of software systems, though they can support each other.

question: Which is a likely risk when restructuring legacy code without adequate understanding or tests?

options.text: All modules become independent automatically
Existing behavior may be altered unintentionally
The system's complexity is guaranteed to disappear
The code becomes reusable by definition

explanation: Insufficient understanding and testing can allow behavior changes or regressions to pass unnoticed.

question: Component-Based Software Engineering (CBSE) emphasizes building systems by:

options.text: Writing every function from scratch for each application
Assembling and integrating independently developed, reusable components
Avoiding component interfaces to simplify integration
Using only components created by the same developer

explanation: CBSE constructs systems from components with defined interfaces, reducing the need to develop every part from scratch.

question: A software component is most useful for reuse when it has:

options.text: Hidden implementation details but no defined interface
Dependencies on undocumented global variables throughout the application
A well-defined interface and limited, understood dependencies
A requirement that its source code be rewritten for every project

explanation: Clear interfaces and manageable dependencies make components easier to understand, integrate, and reuse.

question: In CBSE, a component interface primarily specifies:

options.text: The complete project schedule for the consuming team
Every internal algorithm and private data structure
The services or operations the component exposes and the way clients interact with them
The exact business strategy of every system that uses it

explanation: Interfaces define externally visible services and interaction contracts, not necessarily internal implementation details.

question: Which is a common challenge in component-based development?

options.text: Components can never be tested separately
Reuse always reduces project cost to zero
Components may have mismatched interfaces, assumptions, or non-functional requirements
Component interfaces eliminate all compatibility issues

explanation: Integration can be difficult when components differ in interface, version, performance, security, or assumptions.

question: A team selects an existing authentication component but must adapt its interface and resolve incompatible dependencies. This illustrates that reuse:

options.text: Always costs less than developing a component from scratch
Removes the need for system-level testing
Can involve evaluation, adaptation, integration, and testing costs
Is possible only when the component is open source

explanation: Reused assets can save development effort but still require assessment, adaptation, integration, and validation.

question: Which statement best describes domain engineering?

options.text: Testing a single application after deployment
Rewriting one class to improve its naming
Identifying commonalities and variabilities in a domain to create reusable assets for a family of systems
Converting an application from source code to machine code

explanation: Domain engineering studies a family of related systems and develops reusable domain assets and variation points.

question: Application engineering in a software product-line context primarily involves:

options.text: Removing variability from every product family
Discovering all possible domains without producing applications
Using domain assets and selecting or configuring variants to build a particular application
Replacing reusable assets with unrelated custom code

explanation: Application engineering uses reusable domain assets to produce a specific system for particular requirements.

question: In domain engineering, commonality refers to:

options.text: Features that must differ in every product
A defect shared by all deployed systems
The number of components rejected during integration
Features or characteristics shared across systems in a domain

explanation: Commonality captures what related systems share; variability captures their differences.

question: A software product line supports multiple products from shared core assets. Which concept helps represent features that differ among products?

options.text: Code obfuscation
Business process mapping only
Regression failure
Variability management

explanation: Variability management represents and controls product-specific differences while reusing common assets.

question: Which measure most directly represents the proportion of software functionality or assets obtained through reuse?

options.text: Mean time to repair
Defect density
Cyclomatic complexity
Reuse percentage or reuse ratio

explanation: A reuse ratio estimates the share of a system or its assets that comes from reused material; the exact denominator should be defined.

question: A project contains 30,000 equivalent lines of code, of which 9,000 are reused. If reuse percentage is calculated as reused LOC divided by total equivalent LOC, what is it?
Why should reuse metrics be interpreted carefully when comparing projects?

options.text: Reuse metrics can never be calculated numerically
Reused components always have identical size and quality
A high reuse ratio proves the system has no defects
Projects may define the denominator differently and reused assets can require different adaptation effort

explanation: Metrics are comparable only when their definitions and measurement methods are consistent; reuse quantity alone does not show quality or net savings.

question: Which statement best captures the economic rationale for software reuse?

options.text: Reuse removes all licensing and integration concerns
Reuse guarantees shorter schedules for every project
Reuse is beneficial only if the reused asset is free
Reuse can reduce duplicated development, but benefits depend on acquisition, adaptation, integration, and maintenance costs

explanation: Reuse can avoid repeated development, but its net benefit depends on the full cost and suitability of the reused asset.
